extracted.intended_audience: employers, immigration practitioners, H-1B petitioners, and stakeholders commenting on or implementing H-1B cap selection rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards governing DHS/USCIS implementation of a wage-level-based weighted selection process for H-1B cap registrations and petitions, including required attestations, evidence, timing ('lock-in') of OEWS wage levels, weighting multipliers, and enforcement standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage levels reflect within-occupation comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Wage levels reflect a comparison within an occupation, rather than across occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS recognizes that different occupational classifications carry differing position and wage requirements and that wage levels reflect comparison within an occupation, not across occupations. Thus wage-level comparisons should not be interpreted as directly comparing different SOC occupations (e.g., cardiologists vs. civil engineers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary as a proxy for skill level
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary is generally a reasonable proxy for skill level and correlates with higher skill and higher wage levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS cites data showing median wages increase with LCA wage level (example: Computer and Mathematical Occupations FY2024 medians for Levels I–IV). It accepts salary as an indicator of skill/value placed by employer, while recognizing employers may offer higher wages for competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy objective: prioritize higher-skilled/higher-paid while preserving access
rubrics_metrics.description: The weighted selection process is intended to generally favor allocation of H-1B visas to higher-skilled and higher-paid aliens while maintaining the opportunity for employers to secure H-1B workers at all wage levels and in all eligible occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS states the rule will increase the likelihood that initial H-1B visas go to higher-skilled/higher-paid beneficiaries but will not 'effectively preclude' lower wage levels from participation (explicitly noting level I wages will not be excluded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting multipliers tied to OEWS wage levels (4x/3x/2x/1x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed weighting gives level IV registrations 4x chance, level III 3x, level II 2x, and level I 1x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS explains the multiples correspond to the four OEWS wage levels and were chosen to balance the policy goal of increasing average H-1B skill level (and protecting U.S. workers) with preserving access for employers unable to pay higher wages. DHS rejects claim that the multiples are arbitrary, noting salary correlates with skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant/petitioner must select highest OEWS wage level the proffered wage equals or exceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: On the registration (or petition if registration suspended), the registrant/petitioner must select the highest OEWS wage level that the beneficiary's proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code in the area(s) of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basis for weighting; DHS clarified it will use the OEWS level the proffered wage corresponds to, not LCA level per se, and the form instructions were revised accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: OEWS wage level 'lock-in' at date of registration (unless suspended)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OEWS wage data used to determine the wage level on the registration is 'locked in' as of the date the registration was submitted; if registration is suspended, the OEWS wage level is as of the petition submission date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must select the OEWS wage level corresponding to the registration date even if OEWS data later changes. DHS expects petition evidence to reflect the wage level as of registration; petitioners may provide explanations of any OEWS changes between registration and petition filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required to support selected wage level on Form I-129
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners must submit evidence of the basis of the wage level selected on the registration (e.g., a printout from the DOL OFLC Wage Search website for the beneficiary’s SOC code and area as of the date of registration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form I-129 instructions list required initial evidence when filing an H-1B cap petition in a registration year. The guidance emphasizes using documentation current as of registration and that the petition's wage-level selection should reflect registration-time data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant attestation: registration must represent a bona fide job offer
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants (and petitioners) must attest, under penalty of perjury, that the registration reflects a bona fide job offer and that the employer intends to employ the beneficiary as described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS modified language to require registrants certify that the registration reflects a bona fide job offer; 'bona fide job offer' aligns with definition of 'United States employer' at 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(ii). See new 8 CFR 214.2(h)(10)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS enforcement: denial for filings that manipulate selection odds
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may deny a subsequent new or amended petition filed by the petitioner, or a related entity, on behalf of the same beneficiary if USCIS determines the filing is part of an attempt to unfairly increase the odds of selection (e.g., by reducing the proffered wage to an amount equivalent to a lower wage level than indicated on the original registration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See finalized new 8 CFR 214.2(h)(10)(iii). This is an explicit enforcement tool to address post-selection wage manipulation or other attempts to game the weighted selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-time/full-time adjudication not relevant to selection weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjudication of part-time employment is not relevant in the selection process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS clarified that whether employment is part-time does not affect selection weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of OEWS wage levels for wage and geographic normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of OEWS wage levels for a SOC code within a particular area of intended employment is an effective mechanism for wage and geographic normalization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters supported OEWS as avoiding unfair advantage for employers in certain areas; DHS agrees and relies on OEWS levels as the basis for weighting and normalization across geography and occupations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted selection must have a rational basis under the APA when changing prior approach
rubrics_metrics.description: When changing from a random selection to a wage-based weighted selection, DHS must provide a reasoned explanation and consider reliance interests, alternatives, and the factual record to avoid arbitrary and capricious agency action under the Administrative Procedure Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS argues it reconsidered prior analyses, reviewed comments/evidence, considered alternatives (including the 2020 ranking model), and determined weighting is consistent with statutory authority and policy goals. DHS rejects claims that the change is arbitrary, noting it weighed potential negative impacts and concluded benefits outweigh costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major questions doctrine not triggered for wage-based selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The major questions doctrine applies only in extraordinary cases of transformative expansion of authority; DHS finds the wage-based selection process falls within its traditional role and statutory authority and therefore does not trigger the doctrine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS distinguishes this rule from cases like West Virginia v. EPA, arguing the rule does not restructure the economy or assert a novel unheralded power. DHS cites INA provisions authorizing administration and enforcement of H-1B numerical allocations and related regulatory prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: DHS may consider and reject alternatives but must document consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency should consider alternative selection methodologies and explain why the final approach was chosen; DHS discussed alternatives (including the 2020 ranking approach) and solicited alternatives in the NPRM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS states it explained why it did not adopt the 2020 ranking model and requested potential alternatives in the NPRM; commenters who did not identify viable alternatives provided no basis to prevent finalization. DHS also states potential litigation is not a sufficient reason to avoid finalizing a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting chosen to balance increasing average skill level with access for employers unable to pay higher wages
rubrics_metrics.description: The particular weighting scheme was selected because it advances policy goals (increase average skill level/protect U.S. workers) while balancing competing policy goal of ensuring employers who cannot pay higher proffered wages are not precluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS frames the weighting as an intentional policy tradeoff and defense against claims it simply picks numbers; the scheme aims to 'appropriately balance' interests of U.S. workers, petitioning employers, and alien workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrants/petitioners may explain OEWS changes between registration and petition
rubrics_metrics.description: If OEWS data changes between registration and petition date such that the same proffered wage would correspond to a different wage level, petitioners should still reflect the registration-time wage level on Form I-129 and 'may wish to submit an explanation of any relevant changes in OEWS wage data with the petition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS provides the example where proffered wage corresponded to level IV at registration but OEWS change moved it to level III by petition: petitioner should select level IV on Form I-129 and may submit explanatory documents.
